dedupe_keys.name: communication towers across the greater sage grouse range

description: The U.S. Geological Survey publishes an annual spatial inventory of communication towers across the greater sage-grouse range in the western United States. The February 2026 version describes tower locations and operating periods, including construction and dismantlement dates, for 1985–2025. Records were assembled from four public infrastructure databases and checked against satellite imagery or field visits. The provider page reports 4,322 verified locations plus 794 unverified records and marks the release CC0 1.0, allowing free reuse. Its DOI points to ScienceBase, which displayed a security check during this review; the provider-owned release page and registered metadata were accessible. File formats were not confirmed from that page. The describing paper gives different dates and totals, so users should check version-specific documentation before interpreting completeness. This inventory can support telecom asset exposure, regional network development and environmental-constraint scenarios. It complements data-israel-moep-cellular-antenna-sites in asset type, with different geography and provenance. Tower locations alone do not establish radio coverage, service capacity or network connectivity.
